title: JavaScript WeakMap and WeakSet collections
concepts: Weak references and garbage-collection observability limits
Weak keys and the CanBeHeldWeakly rule
Why weak collections are not enumerable
accuracyFacts: The standardized WeakMap and WeakSet surfaces do not include Symbol.species accessors. The current WeakMap and WeakSet constructor-property clauses specify prototype, while Map and Set have separate species clauses; the ES2015 specification also did not define weak-collection species accessors. Do not teach WeakMap[Symbol.species] or WeakSet[Symbol.species] as real APIs.

CanBeHeldWeakly is true for every Object and for a Symbol only when Symbol.keyFor(symbol) is undefined. This admits non-registered symbols, including well-known symbols, but excludes symbols from Symbol.for. Other primitive values are inadmissible.

For WeakMap, get(nonWeakKey) returns undefined, has(nonWeakKey) returns false, and delete(nonWeakKey) returns false; set, getOrInsert, and getOrInsertComputed throw TypeError for an inadmissible key. WeakSet has/delete return false for inadmissible values, while add throws TypeError.

WeakMap.prototype.getOrInsert returns an existing value even when that value is undefined; otherwise it stores and returns the supplied value. getOrInsertComputed validates the key and callable callback, returns an existing value without calling the callback, otherwise calls callback with the key and undefined this. If the callback mutates this WeakMap for the same key, the algorithm replaces that entry with the computed result before returning it.

WeakMap and WeakSet constructors accept an optional synchronous iterable; WeakMap expects pair-like entries, while WeakSet consumes values. A null or undefined argument creates an empty collection. The constructor retrieves the instance's adder method, so subclass overrides can affect initialization; iteration/adder errors close the iterator when required by the iterable protocol.

Weak collections do not expose size, clear, key/value enumeration, or iterators. This avoids letting program results depend on nondeterministic garbage-collection timing. It does not promise that collection happens immediately when a key loses other references.

WeakMap values may be any JavaScript value. If the key is no longer live, its associated value is also not made live solely by the weak-map entry—even if that value refers back to the key. A separate strong reference to either value or key can change reachability; use weak collections for metadata or membership whose lifetime should follow keys, not as predictable cleanup callbacks.
